People's Majlis Committee Minutes

10th Meeting of the Judiciary Committee

14 October 2026

Venue of the meeting: People's Majlis, G (Committee Room 11)

Start time: 11:15

{Presiding: Committee Chair; Member for Holhudhoo constituency Abdul Sattar Mohamed}

Speech by the Chair:

Bismillahir Rahmanir Raheem. Assalaamu Alaikum. I welcome all honourable members to the 10th meeting of the Judiciary Committee of the People's Majlis. As set out in today's committee agenda, the first item is a discussion of two matters submitted by an honourable member. These are two letters sent by the honourable member for North Galolhu constituency, Mohamed Ibrahim. I believe both of those letters have now been shared with the committee members. The first of them is a letter sent on the matter of finding solutions in connection with the occurrence of accidents. The second is a matter submitted in connection with the Parole Board releasing a person sentenced to 25 years in jail. Then there are also letters sent to the committee by two members of the public. That is in connection with meeting the Judiciary Committee. Then, included under other matters is setting a date to meet the members of the Bar Council, as the honourable members decided at the committee's last meeting, after clarifying the details of it. The Bar Council has now shared those details with this committee. And the Bar Council also wishes to meet the committee. So, the matter of setting a date for that. So, first of all, for items number one and two set on the agenda, I will open the floor to see what the honourable members think about this matter, and to proceed in the way the honourable members decide. So, one and two are the two matters submitted by the honourable member for North Galolhu constituency, Mohamed Ibrahim. The matter of the increase in accidents, and the matter relating to the Parole Board releasing a person sentenced to 25 years in jail; for these two matters, one and two, I will first open the floor, honourable members. So, I will open the floor to the honourable members. Yes! So, I give the floor to the honourable member for Hulhudhoo constituency, Mohamed Shahid.

Speech by the Member for Hulhudhoo constituency Mohamed Shahid:

[stamp]

Yes! Thank you very much, Chair. As we proceed with the committee now that the Majlis has opened for the first time right after this recess, a great many matters have been submitted to the committee. In that regard, we must note something that has recently been a very great concern among us, among the people of the Maldives. The honourable member for North Galolhu constituency, Mohamed Ibrahim, has submitted a matter to this committee. That is, a person sentenced to 25 years in jail in a case of attempting to import 98 kilos of narcotics was released into society. So this member has sent it requesting that we look into and clarify what this release was in that matter, and how this happened. As I understand it, this matter has now been concluded in a certain way by the relevant authority of this government. However, because I consider that disclosing to the Maldivian people through the committee how this happened, or clarifying it to the member who submitted this matter to us, is a duty, a responsibility, of our committee, I consider that looking further into this matter and obtaining information on behalf of this committee is something we must do. Now, some people may think, or some people are saying, for example, that in connection with this, the person released in this matter was released as a result of the way the Parole Board looked into their case and acted. All of those people have now been dismissed. However, that perhaps will not serve the real purpose of this. Both for the Maldivian people and for the party who submitted this matter, how did this come to happen? For example, there are certain principles, certain criteria, for granting parole. There is this Parole Act. So, we would need to establish, wouldn't we, through whose negligence this happened; merely removing the person carrying out that responsibility from that responsibility, or dismissing the person performing that job from the job, does not resolve this. If this is something that happens continually, it must be brought to a stop. Or, if those parties too have committed an offence in this, I believe that looking into and disclosing what offence was committed is something our committee must do. So, I simply propose that our committee look further into and clarify this matter. Thank you.

[stamp]

Speech by the Chair:

I give the floor to the honourable member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed.

Speech by the Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency Ashraf Rasheed:

Thank you, honourable Chair. As the honourable member for Hulhudhoo constituency, Mohamed Shahid, just noted, I too note that this was a very big thing that happened. So, in connection with what happened, according to the information now received, the members of that Parole Board have resigned. However, in resolving problems that arise like this, we must work to find a permanent solution to them. In order for us to clarify how this happened, I think, as member Mohamed Shahid just said and proposed, we should first obtain information, even if by sending a letter to them to obtain the information on how this happened. So, I state that I support it in that way. Then, the other matter on today's agenda, the letter sent in this matter by the honourable member for North Galolhu constituency, Mohamed Ibrahim, the letter sent in connection with dangerous road accidents occurring in the Malé area; according to information I received just before this committee began, a certain decision has been made in connection with this. So, that being so, and since that bill has been passed. Yes! Since it has been passed, I think we should look at that and give a reply, you know; I state that I think we should give a written reply to this letter submitted by Mohamed Ibrahim. Thank you.

Speech by the Chair:

I now give the floor to the honourable member for Kurendhoo constituency, Shamin Habeeb.

Speech by the Member for Kurendhoo constituency Mohamed Shamin Habeeb:

[stamp]

Thank you, Chair. I just want to note that this is the Parole Board matter, you know. Ashraf just noted in it that the Parole Board's board resigned. Did they resign, or were they dismissed? They were dismissed. Now, when a matter like this is submitted, perhaps something we really need to look at is that the person who is always released into society; I do not believe such a dangerous person would be released into society. That is, when we have placed responsible, educationally strong people on boards and in such places, those people would not release a group dangerous to society. So, if someone is released and then taken back again, the problem in it is not the person released. If he is put back in jail again, the problem in it is the people who release. And the way it always goes is that if something goes wrong, that person resigns. Or that person is dismissed. I see no punishment being given. Then another group is put on the board, and they too do wrong again. I do not know at all how many people were released before we arrived at this matter today. That has not been looked into either. How many people has the Parole Board released up to now? In what cases were they released, which people were released? Perhaps that too needs to be looked into, whether these were properly released. If a person who was released is taken back to jail, that is a very big wrong. Those matters will not end merely by resigning or by being dismissed. Meaning, we are giving them the opportunity to do such things in future too. That is, if someone sitting in that place committed an offence, or did this work and did it wrongly, they are dismissed. Once dismissed, the person goes home and it ends there. Then a new group comes. There is no stopping this. In this, we only point the finger at the offenders of society, or at young people who get drawn into crime. That person's name is all over social media. In this matter, I never once see the real reason it had to come to this point being noted and action being taken on it. So, I simply request that this committee look at in what way those people, the people who were removed, how their work went, and why, or else there must also be a way to take action against them too. Otherwise, in this committee we will always only be talking about someone being released, someone being arrested, or social media will always show us doing wrong

[stamp]

and then putting it right again; that is what is seen. That is why in this matter, as Shahid noted, perhaps we need to look at how this matter happened. Then traffic violations; this too is a very big problem. It is causing loss of many people's lives and many injuries. People who offend more than once, people who violate traffic rules, are released into society; they go unpunished. Licences are not suspended. Even when the licence is suspended, they still drive. And even when they drive, there is no way that person can be taken and put in jail. Instead, people are being kept in jail for twenty or thirty days over these small matters. So, to save people's lives and reduce [accidents], accidents can be reduced as much as possible only if the person who drives recklessly even once has the certainty that he will be put in jail and kept there for quite a few days; then he will be very careful. But what happens now is that, for us, the offender's licence is suspended, or if it happens to someone, the licence is suspended; the person who speeds has the licence suspended and is released the next day. Unless strict measures are taken in this way, neither will these accidents decrease. Nor will deaths decrease. So, for this too, for these matters that have been submitted to us, we need to look at this a little more closely; otherwise, I feel the work of this committee is perhaps of no use. We discuss this and go, and it is over. So, I just noted that. Thank you.

Speech by the Chair:

I give the floor to Ahmed Riyaz, the honourable member for Thimarafushi constituency.

Speech by the Member for Thimarafushi constituency Ahmed Riyaz:

Thank you, Chair. Yes. As I understand it, the very first matter now submitted is a matter where this board made a decision. In reality, this board being talked about is a board entrusted with a very great responsibility, a very heavy task. This is a board set up to decide very important matters of the government and the state. Such an act by this board, and in the Maldives

[stamp]

I believe such an act must not be done contrary to the laws and regulations that have been made. Every honourable member appointed to that board must also be people who are very well versed in, and very well aware of, these regulations. The news we get, what we hear from these newspapers and media, is that those people were able to do those things because there was some legal provision for them. But we make the regulations and laws we make so that they are watertight. So, I do not believe there would be any loophole in them. So, in my view, we in the Majlis really need to look into and study this matter very closely. That is, such things being carried out and happening in our country, in our government, is not something we accept. These things must not happen. So, I too fully support what Shahid, Mohamed Shahid, just said. We really want to look into and study these matters. Then, regarding the letter sent about traffic, the letter sent by our honourable member, what I would like to say is that in reality, on the roads in the Maldives now, even on the road I came along just now to come to this Majlis, soldiers and police are standing with barricades set up. The police are standing with cones placed. In reality, I believe no one should be able to lay a hand on any of those. We see, and just now it was seen, a foreigner, an expatriate, when he wanted to drive a pickup he had brought into a restricted place, picked up the cones and moved them aside, drove it in, and then put the cones back himself. These scenes will certainly be clearly visible to the police; those scenes will be visible even from inside their office. Or else they will be on the cameras in all the shops nearby. This footage will be visible. If we keep seeing such things in these small matters and do not stop them, even bigger things than these will happen in future. All these matters of this whole country of ours are run by foreigners. As they please; we Maldivians do not dare to touch a cone and move it aside. How many pickups, how many cars were stopped there just now? But he just moved it aside and went in. So, this

[stamp]

I believe these matters need to be looked into and studied very closely by us, and we in the Majlis too must do everything needed to see whether the parties who must do these things are doing them properly, or else to make those people familiar with them too. So, on this occasion, my opinion on these 2 matters, what I wish to say, is this. Thank you.

Speech by the Chair:

Thank you. I give the floor to the honourable member for Kanditheemu constituency, Ameen Faisal.

Speech by the Member for Kanditheemu constituency Ameen Faisal:

Thank you, Chair. First of all, regarding the letter sent by member Kudoo in connection with this decision made by the Parole Board, I very much support what Shamin said. A person held in jail was in reality released by the Parole Board; was released; was then freed. I cannot believe that something could happen to the point of this person being released, a person held in jail, through contacting the members of this Parole Board or through some conversations with these people, you know. I do not believe, I cannot believe it. However, it has happened. In this, when that offender is taken back to jail again, we must not forget; we really need to look very carefully at how this happened. We must not hesitate, beyond dismissing the board or the board resigning, regarding the responsibility he was entrusted with; if what he did was wrong, the punishment he must receive or whatever else must be done. Otherwise, whatever group is put in a place, whether on a board or a committee, or given some other good job, a responsible job, when he is dismissed for a wrong he does, it ends there; when someone acts in a way that, because of his wrong, causes the loss of the Maldivian people's trust, or the trust of the Maldivian people in that institution, then if that person is guilty through negligence of a responsibility he was entrusted with, he must be found guilty, or if a fine, then fined, or it must be looked into even in a way that he cannot be entrusted with another such responsibility a second time. I believe this is a responsibility of the People's Majlis, a very great responsibility, to see how this happened, how

[stamp]

it came to happen, and to take the strictest action that must be taken against the members who were on that dismissed board. I believe that is something we must do so that in future the decisions this board makes are responsible decisions that the Maldivian people accept, that the people can accept. Secondly, regarding the letter sent about the dangerous accidents occurring on the road, there are very good points in this letter; I too believe that if we in the People's Majlis think deeply about this, talk with the relevant offices and work together, regarding those who lose their lives, or become permanently disabled, or end up needing medical treatment at great expense due to accidents occurring in the Malé area, if we treat it as a responsibility of this Majlis and work jointly with the relevant institutions, a good result could be achieved. Here I just want to note that in this most recent incident too, the person who in reality lost her life was, together with her husband, after finishing work, out for a ride on a motorcycle as a couple for the purpose of relaxing or spending a happy moment, when a dangerous accident happened in Malé on a road where, put another way, one cannot drive at high speed. Most roads in Malé now are not roads where one can drive at high speed. Then, as we learned from social media, this was the fifth time this person had been arrested. So, I cannot believe that the measures now in the regulations, in the law, are measures, punishments, we have written down to really stop offending. When the law or the regulations are written such that one person can be arrested five times for one thing, committing one offence, it means we cannot enforce the provisions in those regulations. That we cannot achieve the result we want from them. We are trying to stop accidents by making a regulation, a law or regulation, on traffic, or on road regulations and driving vehicles. But when a person is arrested five times for the same thing, I cannot believe that what was written in those laws and regulations is working. So, we need to find some other solution to this. Then, member Kudoo also proposed earlier, I believe,

[stamp]

a good solution. Our situation has reached the point of making additional insurance mandatory for driving vehicles in the Malé area. If someone cannot take out insurance for it and pay that amount to an insurance company, they must not drive a vehicle in the Malé area. That is because in many cases, because of the person driving, or when they drive badly, it is often not they who get hurt. The person who drove according to the rules, wholly unconnected to it, loses their life. Because of that, many families have to bear it, have to bear the pain of it. Let us consider an example; I do not know, if that woman who lost her life, that young woman from Sh. Atoll, had a child, or when a father who has a child loses his life in such an accident, let us think of the hardship his parents [unclear] will have to bear for life. A child grows up until 18 and that happened; only a family that feels it will know how painful, difficult and distressing it is. However grown up, when a mother passes away, and especially when a mother passes away in a case like this through someone else's negligence, however grown up that child is, in reality they will feel the absence of the mother. So, that is something we need to think about. Likewise, for example, if something happens from this, especially when a father passes away through someone else's negligence, the hardship and burden that mother bears in raising her children will stay in her heart. In reality, that forgiveness, even if she says she forgives, will not truly happen. That is in reality a very great hardship, a debt. In reality, we must not remain without correcting the provisions in the law when such things happen through carelessness and happen repeatedly. Kudoo has noted very good points in this. In reality, all the roads of the entire Malé area can already be watched by the police through cameras. It is not only when a police officer sees someone driving badly or breaking the rules that action can be taken and the punishment due given. On the bridge too, as we saw, a little while ago when the speed limit was exceeded, an SMS even came. That was something tested and done in the Maldives. So, even when no police officer can be seen, when people driving on Malé's roads break the rules; I too believe this is something seen very often on the roads, especially foreigners coming even against a one-way, on motorcycles, and on bicycles too. Very rarely from Maldivians

[stamp]

or else not seen at all. But something I repeatedly see from foreigners is, when entering a one-way, putting the motorcycle against the one-way. However narrow the road, even if a four-wheeled vehicle came in along that road, he may just come against the one-way. This is not something we see from Maldivians. These are things that can be monitored and acted upon through the CCTV cameras installed in the Malé area and in other ways too. So, we too have a responsibility in this. Day by day, the number of people losing their lives in such road accidents, or in matters connected to them, is increasing. Thank you.

Speech by the Chair:

The honourable member made a very good point, you know. Next, I will give the floor to Ibrahim Nazil, the honourable member for South Hithadhoo constituency.

Speech by the Member for South Hithadhoo constituency Ibrahim Nazil:

Thank you, Chair. As we proceed with this meeting in connection with the issues, or the letters, we have received, I want to start first with the letter we have received in connection with dangerous accidents occurring in the Malé area; as I look at it, in Chapter Two of the law there is Section 6 of the law, determining land transport policy. In order to achieve the objectives of this law, the national land transport policy of the Maldives shall be determined by the President. That is where it starts, at the very top. We have come to this situation today with very many challenges in determining policies. If things the President must do under the President's direct leadership are not completed and are delayed, these matters will get worse day by day. Knowing for certain that every day there are many accidents, that many people, many families are made destitute and helpless, we need to look at what the President has done in connection with this. National Road Safety

[stamp]

Council has been constituted. The people included among the council's members are also set out in the law. The Transport Minister is included, the Finance Minister is included, the Minister of Home Affairs is included, the Minister of Urban Development is included, the Commissioner of Police is included. The most senior heads of institutions, the most senior members of the Cabinet. How much was this discussed in the Cabinet? What action has been taken up to now? According to the Maldives Land Transport Act, we must drive on the left side of a road. But we see that even on a two-way road, four-wheeled vehicles drive on the right side. A traffic police officer is sitting in the middle of the road. That officer does not even signal with his hand to say go on that side even when the other side is empty. That is the situation we are living in. With traffic police and various officials put out on the roads, not even that much is done. Someone wanting to overtake the vehicle in front has to get onto the wrong side. How is this to be done? Getting on like that, driving that way, driving on the road like that has now become fully practised and habitual within Malé. I would say that is exactly the point where the biggest problems of road accidents arise. If the person put out on traffic duty cannot tell people even that much, then there really is a problem in that. It has to be said. He sits right in the middle of the road. Even if police were posted every one thousand feet, one thousand feet, and even increased to every two hundred, two hundred, it would be the same. There would be no change. Why do four-wheeled vehicles have to drive on the right side? There is empty space right on the left side. Then, because the person behind gets no space, that person, even someone on a motorcycle, has to get on and go by overtaking on the left side. In that going, very many things; in reality we cannot even sense it; while in every place in the world vehicles on land are permitted to drive on the right side or the left side, the regulations and standards made for it, overtaking, giving signals, and when stopping at places where one must stop to give way to people crossing the road, when one has stopped on the wrong side, the things that will then happen are in reality very serious matters. In this regard, as I said, what work has the National Road Safety Council done? Their responsibility is in the law. The President's responsibility is there. On this, we keep repeating, repeating this same talk

[stamp]

we are talking. Talking and talking, I see no solution coming to this. I see no action being taken by the government on this. I want to propose that the Traffic Police be summoned to this committee, [to see] together with the Traffic Police what things we can do to resolve this. We say this because the Traffic Police are directly the people who can best do this in reality, who can give the public support in doing this, or make the public familiar with it. In addition, I want to know what the National Road Safety Council has done in connection with this up to now, what discussions were held? What discussions in the Cabinet, what advice was given to the President? It is the President who is entrusted with deciding. It is the President's Cabinet ministers who are there to advise the President. What advice was given to the President by these people? What advice was given? Because I consider that is information we need to know today, information this committee needs to know, I propose, as a proposal, that we bring the Traffic Police to this committee and that we consult with them. In addition, what is the advice the National Road Safety Council gave the President? If advice has been given, at what point will the President take action in connection with it? Thank you for the opportunity.

Speech by the Chair:

I now give the floor to Mohamed Shahid, the honourable member for Hulhudhoo constituency.

Speech by the Member for Hulhudhoo constituency Mohamed Shahid:

Thank you, you know, Chair. Just before going to the second matter of today, it occurred to me that, regarding the second matter, the debate on the matter noted as the second item of the agenda is going ahead. As it goes on, the honourable member for North Galolhu constituency, Mohamed Ibrahim, has also submitted this matter to the committee. Then, I very strongly disagree with what the honourable member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil, just said in the committee. The reason is that we

[stamp]

every Maldivian citizen would be very saddened and grieve; we grieve every tragic incident that befalls every Maldivian citizen. And whether harm comes to someone through an assault being committed, through a murder being committed, or even if that person passes away, we grieve in that case too.

Speech by the Chair:

We will continue after the call to prayer has finished.

Speech by the Member for Hulhudhoo constituency Mohamed Shahid:

Yes! I will pause for the call to prayer.

Speech by the Chair:

(Committee paused for the call to prayer) Please continue!

Speech by the Member for Hulhudhoo constituency Mohamed Shahid:

Yes! I disagree because, in the way the honourable member for South Hithadhoo constituency, Ibrahim Nazil, framed his remarks, it seemed as though, now that this state has been running for three years, he spoke in a way that implied that by this point the state has taken no measures of any kind on this. And likewise, that such things happen because of laxity in running the government. However, I must note that there is no government that works more than this one for the rights of the Maldivian nation and people, to provide the people with protection and safety. That will be very well known, won't it, since even the coming into existence of such a law came about under today's government; as the honourable [member] said, Section 6 of this law states that, in order to achieve the objectives of this law, the national land transport policy of the Maldives shall be determined by the President. So, such a law came into existence under this government, along with the increase in the recurrence of these very matters. Along with that, we need to think that our individual responsibility in this is also very great, you know. As things are arranged in our Maldives, especially, the governing

[stamp]

island [of the Maldives] is Malé. All the people of the Maldives have gathered in Malé. There are no big roads here of the kind you speak of, with traffic police standing to direct people from right to left, from left to right; there is not even a road for that. There is not even a place to park. To resolve these matters, to secure the safety and security of these roads, a great deal of work is being done even up to today to establish a parking system and to provide all these conveniences to the Maldivian people. And accidents are not happening for lack of a law. Nor are offenders offending for that reason. Even now I remember that among us, before this too, there was this third-party insurance. There was road worthiness. It was you people who opposed all of these things, you know. Whenever the Maldivian government brings any such thing for the people, you people say that when our government comes we will abolish all these things. As if the small bit of money that goes from the people at that moment, the small bit of money to be paid for third-party insurance, the small bit of money to be paid for road worthiness, we will waive it. So, there is no need to do it. You people oppose every such thing. It is also because of you people that obstacles are placed in the work today's government is doing to provide the Maldivian people with this safety and security, which harms Maldivian citizens. Even in this parking matter, on driving more than a certain number at once on Malé's roads and such things, even when roads are closed and it is made so that one cannot drive on that road during school hours, you people come out and even protest. You people come out onto the roads and shout, saying it is to hold the government accountable, against it. So, first of all, we need to shoulder our own individual responsibility too, you know. Then, as you said, someone remaining released after offending four times, five times, is a problem. I too support that. I fully support honourable member Nazil. And I also support Ameen. That must not be so. When someone has been arrested and released four or five times in one matter and such things start happening on his part, we need to look into those matters. To look into such matters, the best thing for this committee is to look at how that release happened. In no way has the honourable member submitted this because this law does not exist. This is not newly being created; what his letter states, what has been sent to this place, to this committee, is that these matters even now

[stamp]

are things being acted upon. We must all follow all of these things. When driving, we should drive carefully. When parking, we should be careful. We should not go breaking one-ways. We are importing vehicles into Malé in great numbers. As soon as steps begin to be taken to work on stopping imports, you people say that under our government you will be able to park as much as you like. You will be able to register. Look! When our government came, what existed under your government was that people were allowed to bring in as many pickups, lorries and vans as they liked, and all these companies were also allowed. Under you people, every four-wheeled thing was released to WAMCO, to RDC, to MTCC so that you would get seventy-five thousand, one hundred thousand rufiyaa, two hundred thousand rufiyaa a month. This is the reason these vehicles increased in Malé. This is the reason these vehicles increased. This is what made things difficult for the people. This is what became hard. This is why accidents increased. This is why parking became difficult. When we started work to resolve these matters, you people came out and protested that every Maldivian citizen must be able to register, even a hundred per head. They must be able to import too. They must be able to register too. So, in such important matters connected with the people, I say with great respect that you too, as the leader of the MDP's parliamentary group, the Minority Leader, are on this committee of ours. So, together with your support too, we very much request that the Maldivian people be advised and made aware in such matters, so that those people do not take part in such things; meaning, to advise those people not to encourage them in the things they do against this traffic violation [matter]; and when you take a leading part in your party's affairs too, and particularly when speaking in the Majlis, I very much request that you speak in this direction. In no way is it for lack of a regulation or law. Nor is it because no measures are taken on those matters, or because they are not acted upon. Even now we see very well that, for example, in Malé, a big road is Majeedhee Magu. Every five feet, five feet there is a police officer, whether traffic or ordinary police. But that officer signals, for example, that there is no way through here, or a barrier [unclear]. He will signal with his hand to move to this side. Fine, not a single person even stops. Not even stopping. He just drives on. Even while he is going holding [him] in his hand

[stamp]

he still goes. Then, for example, stopping that motorcycle, it was towed. For example, when a motorcycle is towed for fifteen days for not having a licence, when the person driving without a licence is arrested and the motorcycle is towed, how many people go to the police. Now the traffic talk is: I have even been fined. My motorcycle or car has been towed. I must get it back today itself. I must say with regret that very many honourable members of this Majlis of ours also face this hardship and difficulty. These people too call the police as soon as they are called. Such-and-such a youngster from my constituency just had his car taken away while it was parked here. Release it quickly. I am giving an example. This is not talk of releasing. We, being members, would not even call like that. Nor could it be released by calling. Nor would they do it. Nor must it be done. However, from where we stand, from this point, we need to think about these matters. A nation will progress properly only when it gets better, when everyone becomes disciplined, with everyone supporting all such things. There is nothing in this to call opposition or government. Nothing to call a particular party. However good a thing the government does, today you people, the political leaders who belong to you, in order to weaken the government, explain every such thing to the people the opposite way. The result is that all the hardship and destitution from it falls upon, confronts and harms the ordinary, destitute people. Those destitute people are now thinking about the things being said by political parties, by senior figures. That is, what we saw before this was that the people just went whichever way the senior political leaders said, whether it was right or wrong; they were misled into going whichever way those leaders said. However, the Maldivian people now think very much about such matters. So, I too fully support that all possible work must be done to resolve these matters. [They] must also be summoned. Work must also be done to further strengthen these matters. However, I truly believe that our government, led by the honourable President, is paying very great attention to such matters and doing a great deal of work to prevent such things from happening further. Shahid's proposal was supported by honourable member Ashraf Rasheed, the honourable member for Faresmaathodaa constituency. So, I ask the honourable members who agree to clarify this information and to summon the members of the Parole Board to vote. (Voting) Ah! I will open the floor, you know. Yes! Thank you. So, I will put to a vote the matter in agenda item number one, and the proposal made on the matter connected with item number one. That is, what honourable member Ibrahim Nazil proposed is to summon the Traffic Police to this committee. So, honourable members who agree with that; who supported that proposal? Yes! The first to support that proposal was Mohamed Shahid, the honourable member for Hulhudhoo constituency. After that, Ismail Nizar also supported it. So, I ask the honourable members who agree with that to vote. (Voting) Yes! Thank you. So, I declare that summoning the Traffic Police has passed by consensus of the committee. in the matter of bringing in the members, as the honourable members just expressed, since that board does not exist at this time, whom shall we summon? I will reopen the floor on that. I give the floor to Ashraf Rasheed, the honourable member for Faresmaathodaa constituency.

Speech by the Chair:
Yes! I give the floor to Hassan Waheed, the honourable member for Vilufushi constituency.

Speech by the Member for Vilufushi constituency Hassan Waheed:
Thank you, Chair. I too believe that there is no such board now. Those people have been dismissed. So, I support the proposal made by the honourable member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf, to proceed with it that way.

So then, honourable, with no views from other honourable members, the proposal now submitted, as it stands, which was proposed by the honourable member for Faresmaathodaa constituency, Ashraf Rasheed, and supported by the honourable member for Vilufushi constituency, Hassan Waheed, is, with there being no Parole Board now, to first bring information in writing in connection with the matter first submitted.
